root_idea.summary: The root centers on taking or handling something and passing it from one party to another.
root_idea.development: The lexical development extends from reaching out to take by hand, to handing over and giving, mutual exchange, gifts, and figurative undertaking.

qac_form_accounting.reason: A distinct Quran-attested verb occurring in 54:29.
A distinct Quran-attested nominal meaning gift or bestowal.

senses.definition: To reach out to take up or seize something, and thereby undertake an act; in the Quranic use, to advance against the she-camel and strike it.
senses.usage_conditions: In 54:29, the expression is explained as raising oneself and the hands to take the she-camel or a sword and then killing; it is also interpreted as emboldening oneself to undertake the act.

senses.definition: To give, present, offer, deliver, or bestow something to a recipient.
senses.usage_conditions: The action denotes giving or delivery and does not require the recipient actually to take or receive the thing. In the Quran it includes giving an owed levy as well as granting, assigning, or bestowing a benefit.

senses.definition: A gift, benefaction, grant, provision, or bestowal.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quran this is the bestowed benefit or reward itself, rather than merely the act of giving; it may be attributed to God or described as an enduring or unrestricted grant.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To stretch or reach upward toward something in order to take it, especially by raising the head or hands.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a gazelle or kid reaching toward tree leaves, and of the corresponding active participle; the same physical reaching may be expressed by taking with the hand.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To serve, render service, or minister to someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The derived verb can describe one who has the office of serving another.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To incite someone to hasten or make haste.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a causative use distinct from the intransitive use of hastening.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To hasten or make haste.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A derived intransitive use describing the subject's own haste.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To hand or pass something to another, mutually or reciprocally; to work for someone and hand over what is wanted.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression can describe reciprocal passing or presenting, including the passing of drinks among companions.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A prohibited face-to-face exchange of swordplay in which each party brings the other’s sword near and they engage one another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a specialized conventional use referring to a staged or mutually enacted sword encounter.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be tractable, manageable, submissive, or yielding rather than resisting.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Of a camel, it means giving its head and not resisting; of a person, giving the hand can express submission; of a bow, it means bending readily and being pliable.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To take something that has been presented or offered, especially by hand.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The object may be food, drink, a vessel, or another thing; the construction corresponds to taking or handling with the hand.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To take or appropriate something that is not rightfully due.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is the morally negative use of taking what one has no right to take.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To contend with one another in taking or giving, each passing or attempting to take something from the other.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression can include overcoming or surpassing another in the reciprocal act.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To recite verses or poetry in turn, or vie with one another in recitation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension of reciprocal exchange, especially used of the rajaz metre.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To venture upon, undertake, or engage in something boldly and without hesitation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: It may refer to a noble or honorable undertaking, or specifically to embarking on a bad or foul act; it can also describe taking up activities such as wine-drinking or gambling.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To affect or attempt a skill or status one does not possess.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of pretending to be a poet or attempting eloquence without being qualified for it.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To ask, demand, or seek a gift from people.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The request may be made with or into the hand, emphasizing the gesture of begging or asking for a gift.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The act of giving, especially liberal, bountiful, munificent, or generous giving.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The related intensive designation مِعْطَاءٌ describes a person who gives much or often; this is an intensive description of the same giving branch, not a separate Quranic form.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A stipend, pay, or allowance issued from a government treasury or assigned to soldiers or others.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term may refer to a regular governmental disbursement, distinguished in some usages from periodic sustenance or رزق.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To reach for or claim what one does not possess or what cannot reasonably be attained.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The proverb may describe arrogating property or knowledge without the means or discipline to support the claim.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A large quantity of thin excrement, in the expression أَلْقَى عَطَوِيًّا.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is an idiomatic and rare usage associated with the reported story behind the expression.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The name of a Kharijite sect, named in relation to ʿAṭiyyah ibn al-Aswad.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A proper-name designation rather than a productive general lexical sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A hand-mill or millstone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized lexical expression meaning the hand-mill, synonymous with الرَّحَى.
